items.title: Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 23, 2003 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: He was a big Gene Krupa fan. And when he heard him that night, his eyes— he said boy this guy can play.

ctx.x: You’ve played almost with everybody. I’m wondering if there’s anybody that you felt you missed.

Well I missed Bing Crosby. I never played for Bing. I wish I had but that’s a great history there. Eddie Lang played for him. But I followed him every step of the way. I heard all the records that he made and I always enjoy them. And the next best thing was Frank. And I made some records with him. I played at the White House with Frank and Perry Como. And we put a program together for Reagan, you do this and you do that and we had fun putting it together. Same with Benny. Benny had no music with the sextet. We…
Is there something generally in your career that you are most proud of?

items.title: Ruth & Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Saddle River, New Jersey, January 19, 2015
items.q: My mother gave us a little trouble, because he was a musician, and marijuana was in the thing. And Gene Krupa.

ctx.x: I thought we’d get a couple of those moments here. Okay so Ruth, how did you meet?

I was a registered nurse at St. Joseph’s Hospital in Paterson, New Jersey, and I had just graduated. It was in 1951, ’52, something like that. And I happened to look — I was on duty and I happened to look up, and sitting on the bench, they had a little bench outside the admitting department. And I had to go out and say, “may I help you.” So I walked out and this wonderful looking man, oh beautifully dressed, and I went out and I said, “may I help you.” And he said, “I’m waiting for my sister, Marie Pizzarelli.”…

you’re a celebrity and you worked with Vaughan Monroe, my favorite, my sister and I.” It was bliss. And so after that I was still living in the nursing school home and the phone rang while I was waiting for my brother to come pick me up to go home. And the phone rang, and it was Marie saying, and I happened to be there — I went to the phone, Marie said, “oh Ruth, my brother wants to talk to you” meaning Mr. Pizzarelli. He said, “hi Ruth, would you like to go out tonight?” I said, “oh I’d love to but I can’t go…
